title: Phantom vibration syndrome — your phone buzzes when it isn't
voiceover: You feel your phone buzz in your pocket. You reach for it. There's no notification. The phone never buzzed. This happens to about 90 percent of people who carry a phone, and it has a name. Phantom vibration syndrome. Your brain has become so trained to expect notifications that it starts inventing them. Any sensation in the area — fabric shifting, muscle twitch, even your heartbeat — gets misread as a buzz. The wild part is it's gotten more common as phones got better. Your brain is now hallucinating your phone before it even rings. Follow Mindbloom for one fact a day.
